newsitem.title: GERMANY: Prodi sees consequences if Italy EMU start delayed.
newsitem.headline: Prodi sees consequences if Italy EMU start delayed.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Monday there would be serious consequences if Italy was not in the European economic and monetary union from its planned 1999 start date.

"I don't know what will happen to the lira (in such a situation)...and the successful effort of curbing inflation may be endangered," he told a news briefing ahead of a meeting of German business leaders in Frankfurt.
Prodi also said that Italy was moving in the right direction to meet the Maastricht Treaty criteria on debt levels for EMU entry.

"Everyone knows the debt criteria won't be met by anyone. The Maastricht Treaty stresses the trend is the important thing. We're trying to go in the trend, and from this point of view I will meet the criteria," he said.
The Maastricht criteria for EMU entry require countries to reduce their public debt levels to 60 percent of gross domestic product or show significant progress in that direction.
A Reuters survey published on Wednesday showed that economists around Europe only expect three countries -- Luxembourg, France and Britain -- to strictly meet the guidelines for debt.

Prodi had said earlier after talks in Munich with Bavarian prime minister Edmund Stoiber that he would not ask for a weakening of the criteria for EMU and that there was no need to delay Italy's entry.
"I fully trust the fact that Italy be ready for next spring. I won't ask for any delay of Italy's EMU entry," Prodi said.
